hero.title: Kolabr vs ClickUp
hero.lede: ClickUp gives your team one place to manage everything. Kolabr gives your team and your guests one place to get it done together: everyone who needs a say is in the channel, free, able to ask, approve and talk, and nobody needs a tour of a workspace to find their way.

room.title: How many guests your users can bring in
room.lede: On ClickUp, a guest who can comment or approve needs a guest place, and how many places you get depends on how many users you pay for. On Kolabr, guests are never counted.

items.title: Are ClickUp guests free?
items.body: Some are. A view-only guest is free and unlimited, but cannot comment, approve or edit. A guest who can do any of those takes a guest place. On Unlimited you get 5 places for your first user and 2 for each user after that; on Business, 10 and then 5. Past that, inviting another one adds a paid seat to your bill. People on your own email domain cannot be guests at all. In Kolabr every guest can post, raise requests, read the wiki and join calls, free, on every plan.

items.title: ClickUp has chat and calls now. What is different?
items.body: Its chat and calls are good, and they are not the difference. What changes is who gets a say. On ClickUp every guest who can comment or approve uses a guest place, and past your allowance each one costs a paid seat, so teams ration who they invite. In Kolabr every guest takes part, free. And a guest opens one channel rather than a workspace, with requests that carry a response target they can hold you to.

items.title: Where are the boards and Gantt charts?
items.body: Kolabr does not have them, by design. They are planning views for your team. What a guest needs is the request: who has it, where it is and when it is due, kept up to date without anybody redrawing a chart. If your team plans delivery on a board, keep that board. The promise lives in the request.

items.title: Which is cheaper?
items.body: It turns on whether your guests take part. Per user, ClickUp Unlimited is $7 a month on yearly terms and Kolabr Pro is $8.50, so while your guests only watch, ClickUp Unlimited is the smaller bill. Once more guests need a say than your allowance covers, every 2 more add a paid seat and the bill soon passes ours. ClickUp Business makes room for more guests, but at $12 a user it costs more than Kolabr Pro from the first user. The chart above works it out for your number of users.

items.title: We have built a lot in ClickUp. Is that wasted?
items.body: Not at all, and it is a reason to keep it for internal delivery. The usual approach is to leave the build where it is and open Kolabr channels for the client-facing side, where the conversation, the requests and the wiki need to be somewhere guests can be without a seat or a licence.

proof.title: Proof takes one week
proof.lede: Open a channel for one client and invite everyone on their side who has ever had a question. There is no seat arithmetic to do first.

steps.text: Invite the whole client team, including the people you would never have spent a guest seat on. Nothing to configure, nothing to approve.
Requests are arriving from the people who actually have them, with the detail attached, instead of through one contact who summarises.
You will know how much of your week used to go on relaying. That is the only test this page is asking you to run.

cta.title: Let your guests do more than watch.
cta.body: Free for one channel, no card. Seven days on Pro or Business when you want the rest. Open a channel and invite everyone on their side, because it costs nothing.
